title: Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari — a declared absence: fourteen works named, with their rights holders and the dates they open, beside the precursors they read (27/01–27/06)
edition: No edition held. The seat holds the declaration of what it would hold: declared/absence.json and declared/absence.md.

license.payload: The declaration is the archive's own, CC-BY-4.0. The works it names are in copyright: Les Éditions de Minuit, Presses Universitaires de France, François Maspero, Éditions Galilée and the authors' estates.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization: None: the declaration is held as written.
scope: Declared, not seated: Gilles Deleuze, Empirisme et subjectivité (Presses Universitaires de France, 1953), opens in the United States on 2049-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Nietzsche et la philosophie (Presses Universitaires de France, 1962), opens in the United States on 2058-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Le Bergsonisme (Presses Universitaires de France, 1966), opens in the United States on 2062-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Différence et répétition (Presses Universitaires de France, 1968), opens in the United States on 2064-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Spinoza et le problème de l'expression (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1968), opens in the United States on 2064-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Logique du sens (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1969), opens in the United States on 2065-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Spinoza: philosophie pratique (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1981), opens in the United States on 2077-01-01; Gilles Deleuze, Le Pli: Leibniz et le baroque (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1988), opens in the United States on 2084-01-01; Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari, L'Anti-Œdipe (Capitalisme et schizophrénie 1) (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1972), opens in the United States on 2068-01-01; Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari, Kafka: pour une littérature mineure (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1975), opens in the United States on 2071-01-01; Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari, Mille plateaux (Capitalisme et schizophrénie 2) (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1980), opens in the United States on 2076-01-01; Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari, Qu'est-ce que la philosophie ? (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1991), opens in the United States on 2087-01-01; Félix Guattari, Psychanalyse et transversalité (François Maspero, 1972), opens in the United States on 2068-01-01; Félix Guattari, Chaosmose (Éditions Galilée, 1992), opens in the United States on 2088-01-01. Deleuze's courses at Vincennes and Saint-Denis (1971–1987): the recordings and the transcriptions (WebDeleuze; the Purdue Deleuze Seminars) are published by permission of the estate, under no open licence; not seated.

why_seated: MANUS, 27 October 2026, after the twenty-sixth seating: "deleuze and guattari... no way around that copyright, huh?" Told that every route through it is closed for decades, and offered a declared absence for them and the open sources they read: "yes - i cant believe we havent seated spinoza yet. yes to all" — and "and leibniz' monadology only". Deleuze and Guattari are entered as an absence because no route through their copyright is open: Guattari's works open in France on 1 January 2063, Deleuze's and the joint works on 1 January 2066, and the books in the United States between 2049 and 2088. The seat states what is missing and why, beside the six seats of the sources they read.
ruling: A declared absence: the works named, with rights holders and opening dates, and no text (MANUS, 2026-10-27).
